speaker_role: current admissions officer (director of admission, Pitzer College)
commercial_incentive: None evident - official college-produced advice video
key_insights: Demonstrated interest includes campus visits, virtual information sessions, interviews, and even passive engagement like opening emails or clicking links
Pitzer frames demonstrated interest not as a checklist to complete but as a way for applicants to learn about the institution and decide if it's the right fit
The college's outreach (emails, interviews, info sessions) is meant to convey its core values so applicants can reflect that understanding in their essays
Engaging with these touchpoints can help an applicant's essay show genuine alignment with the school's stated values
notable_or_distinctive: Directly from a college's own admissions office (Pitzer), it explicitly reframes 'demonstrated interest' as knowledge-gathering for the student rather than a scored checklist, which is a notably student-centered framing distinct from most demonstrated-interest advice.
reliability_notes: Very short, promotional-style video specific to one college (Pitzer); general framing may not apply to schools that formally track and score demonstrated interest differently.
